findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: `counter-case` conflates the steel-man with the right of reply, and the only alternative field is dead by the schema's own test
findings.expected: An accused party's own published response is held as sourced, quotable evidence with an attribution and a locator, separable from the author-constructed steel-man, and consumed by the composition procedure as a party position rather than as the case against the author's verdict.
findings.got: One column ('the strongest argument that nothing unusual is happening') wired to one field defined as 'the strongest case against the verdict'. The worked run files the accused party's own defence (f-mstr-defence) into counter-case and consumes it as steel-man evidence, whose statement is authored prose, then scores it down in the render. The second candidate field, `counter_positions_to_state_fairly[]`, is declared with no shape and is absent from the consumed-by table — which by the schema's own principle means it does not belong in the schema.
findings.lens_argument: A new column holds the material but does not change the steel-man's ROLE, which is load-bearing in Engines A and D (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:65-66; ENGINES.md:94-96). Making a right of reply first-class requires the notebook to model two parties and a record where it today models one author and their best objection — a shared-mechanism change, not a row edit. CEILING: even a lens as the skill specifies one (search-domains/dimensions/evidence-floor/engine-affinity/conclusion-policy/exposure-class) has no slot for a party structure, so adopting this needs a schema change plus a lens carrying the policy.
findings.refuter_pass: Not topic-specific: every seat with a named accused party (crypto-collapse, public-sector corruption, consumer scam) is downstream of the same column. Competent execution makes it worse, not better — a researcher who correctly files the rebuttal in counter_positions_to_state_fairly writes it into a field no composition step reads.
findings.l2_priority: Produce a notebook for a two-party dispute and check where the accused's own words physically land, whether they survive into the rendered script attributed and quoted, and whether the render scores them.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: `verdict`'s authoring time is unspecified, and `steel_man` is defined relative to it — D-rigged tell 2 fails by construction
findings.expected: The prompt pins when `verdict` is written relative to Phase 6, or requires the verdict be re-tested against the steel-man before the notebook closes, so the opposition is not constructed as the complement of a fixed answer.
findings.got: `verdict` is required to be 'written during research, not during scripting' and is assigned to no phase in the 1-9 sequence; `steel_man` is defined as 'the strongest case against the verdict'. In the ordering the prompt permits, the answer is fixed before the opposition is read. The worked render's own honesty table marks tell 2 as passing, while candidate 4's heading is 'Verdict — and the reason this is the answer'.
findings.refuter_pass: By design? 'Answer early' is a craft commitment (CRAFT-BASELINE.md:92-99) — but that governs the script's delivery order, not the research's authoring order, and conflating the two is the error. Cheapest fix in the report: pin the phase.
findings.l2_priority: Record the wall-clock order in which `verdict` and `steel_man` were authored, and run the control arm: re-derive the verdict after the steel-man and see whether it changes.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: The `unhinged` tier permits a motive claim about a named living individual, with no gate on the subject
findings.expected: A leap ceiling that depends on who the claim is about: when the subject is a named living individual, the ceiling drops and the claim is about conduct, not knowledge. A `subject`/`names_individual` field, and an exposure class.
findings.got: `unhinged` is DEFINED as 'a claim about MOTIVE'. The `Conclusion` interface has no subject, no naming rule, no exposure field. `hottest` is a rendering badge, not an authoring constraint. The worked example asserts motive about identifiable officeholders; nothing distinguishes that from the same sentence with a named executive in the subject position.
findings.refuter_pass: The orchestrator asked whether the falsifier requirement already constrains this adequately. It constrains it PARTIALLY and deserves credit: every motive claim must nominate a test. It does not constrain WHO the claim is about, and a document-shaped falsifier on a defamatory motive claim mitigates damages rather than preventing publication. No naming rule exists in conclusions.ts, NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md, RESEARCH-PROMPT.md or ENGINES.md.
findings.l2_priority: Generate conclusions on a two-party dispute and count how many reach `far`/`unhinged` with a named individual as subject without any prompt discouraging it.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: `falsifiableBy: string` is unconstrained — a mental-state falsifier satisfies the type and the quality bar
findings.expected: A falsifier constrained to a thing that could exist and be produced — a filing, a restatement, a verdict, a measurement. Something like `falsifierKind: 'document' | 'record' | 'measurement'`, checked at authoring time.
findings.got: A required free string. 'Wrong if their intent was different' satisfies the type, satisfies the header note's literal words, and is untouched by the quality bar, which does not mention falsifiers at all. Checkability is only tested downstream by a human reviewer at L2.
findings.refuter_pass: Would competent execution produce a document falsifier anyway? In the worked run, yes — 7/7, genuinely exemplary, and credited in the report. But the quality-bar checklist never checks a falsifier, so the good practice is unenforced habit rather than a property of the artifact. The value is present; the constraint is absent.
findings.l2_priority: Score every produced falsifier as document / record / measurement / mental-state and report the count.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: No locator on `facts[].source`, and `sources[]` is not joined to facts
findings.expected: Every allegation traces to a document, a page and a line: a structured source with kind, identifier, date and locator, joined to the fact it supports.
findings.got: `facts[] = {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?}` where `source` is free text, and a flat `sources[]` URL list unattached to any fact. The worked notebook's first fact is `load_bearing: true` and sourced to two aggregators with no locator. Secondary sourcing on a fraud allegation is a liability the schema cannot express.
findings.refuter_pass: Partly my topic being hard — locator discipline matters more in filings work than in market commentary. But every seat citing a primary document (legislative analysis, security advisories, box office) needs the same field, and the defect already bit the founding topic on a load-bearing fact. High reachability.
findings.l2_priority: Count produced facts whose source is a primary document with a retrievable locator versus an aggregator.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: 'Vendor research is low by default' conflates an interested source with an unreliable one, and there is no field for a disclosed position
findings.expected: Reliability and interest recorded on separate axes: a short report is advocacy with a disclosed position whose arithmetic is often correct and independently reproducible from the filings. The disclosure itself recorded as a fact, and Phase 1 asked to retrieve it.
findings.got: A single three-value `confidence` scale with vendor research demoted by default, no source-interest field anywhere, and no Phase-1 row asking for the source's position. Quoting a short report's numbers without its position disclosure is neither prevented nor prompted against. The only disclosure obligation in the methodic belongs to one engine and is lost on re-render.
findings.refuter_pass: By design? The rule exists to prevent 'laundered confidence' and is right about that risk. It is still the wrong axis: reliability and interest are orthogonal. Note also that the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder is a knowledge-library contract for craft claims and is NOT applied to notebook facts at all — which partially disposes of the orchestrator's evidence-ladder hypothesis for this seat: the ladder is not in the room.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt to record an interested source's correct figure and see which confidence value the prompt drives it to.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud

findings.title: `macro.emptyMeans` is false for entity-level topics — correct restraint is badged as a gap
findings.expected: An `emptyMeans` that is true in the domain, or a per-topic way to mark a column not-applicable.
findings.got: An empty `macro` column asserts 'the asset is being explained in isolation from the market it trades in'. For a company-specific accounting dispute the column is correctly empty; the `emptyMeans` contract converts that into a badged defect. An `emptyMeans` is a claim about meaning, and this one is untrue outside markets.
findings.refuter_pass: There is no mechanism anywhere to mark a dimension not-applicable for a topic, so this cannot be routed around by a careful researcher. Held to minor: it misleads a reviewer, it does not corrupt an output.

findings.title: No column for the assurance trail, and none for chronology — both fall through DEFAULT_DIMENSION
findings.expected: A column for the reliability of the evidence base itself (auditor opinion, control qualifications, auditor change, restatement history), and a time axis for filing dates against disclosure dates against trading dates.
findings.got: Orphan groups O3 and O4. Both land in 'The number' via `DEFAULT_DIMENSION`, where a reviewer looking for the audit history would never look — the exact failure the file's own comment documents having already happened once on the founding run.
findings.refuter_pass: Chronology is generic — every OSINT and breaking-news seat needs a time axis, so expect convergence there. The assurance trail is mine and one or two adjacent fraud seats, so it ranks lower on frequency. Related to but distinct from the pre-recorded G-000: this is a whole CLASS of material with no column, not an untagged card.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether a live fraud notebook produces assurance-trail and chronology facts, and where the board would put them.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: Exposure has no home in the durable artifact
findings.expected: An exposure field on the notebook and on each conclusion — what being wrong costs, who is named, what a lawyer or editor would say — so the assessment travels with the asset across renders.
findings.got: The rubric scores `exposure` as one of eight dimensions and the notebook has no field for it: not on `facts[]`, not on `Conclusion`, not at the top level. Exposure is assessed in review and stored nowhere, under a philosophy in which the notebook is the asset and the script is disposable.
findings.refuter_pass: Possibly deliberate for a market-derived methodic — which is the point rather than a defence: exposure is invisible to a methodic derived from a topic with no people in it, and the skill says exactly that about itself. Expect convergence from geopolitics and public-sector seats.
findings.l2_priority: Attempt an exposure review on a produced notebook and record where the assessment had to be written instead.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: 'The mechanics are established and the intent is unestablished' is not a first-class position — no leap tier for withholding, no column, no engine
findings.expected: A non-settlement position that can be gated, ranked, linked by `restsOn` and wounded by descoping like any other claim; visible on the board; renderable by at least one engine.
findings.got: Expressible in `verdict` and — better than expected — in `unknowns[].impact`, which explicitly tells the script what it may not say. But there is no `unknowns` column in DIMENSIONS, so it is invisible at triage; `Leap` runs near -> unhinged with every rung a rung forward and no register for withholding; and Engine D's viewer pleasure is 'watching a question get settled', with SCQA and the reframe ending both pushing toward resolution.
findings.refuter_pass: Checked before complaining, and half of the fear was unfounded: `unknowns[].impact` is a genuinely good instrument and the `verdict` field can hold the sentence. Engine A may also carry it — 'the mechanics are exactly as alleged, and that is where the evidence stops' is a real reversal — so severity is held to minor and the engine half is `undecided` rather than asserted. What remains confirmed: no board visibility, no conclusion register, no gating.
findings.l2_priority: Write the non-settlement verdict into a live notebook and see whether any engine renders it without converting it into a ruling.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud

findings.title: The only author-exposure disclosure obligation lives inside one engine and evaporates on re-render
findings.expected: Disclosure of the author's position recorded in the notebook, so it survives every render — consistent with 'notebook is the asset, script is a disposable render'.
findings.got: Engine E requires a Briefing to 'disclose the author's exposure'. It is the only such obligation in the methodic. Re-render the same notebook through A or D and it is gone, because it was never in the durable artifact. Flagged for the philosophy bench.
findings.refuter_pass: Present but missed? Searched prompt, schema, dimensions, conclusions and craft baseline — it appears exactly once, in one engine's distinctive obligations. Confirmed as a placement defect, not a discoverability one.
findings.l2_priority: Render one notebook through two engines and check which honesty obligations survive the second render.

findings.creator: public-co-fraud
findings.topic: adjudicating a published short-seller report against a listed company's published rebuttal, on the filings
findings.title: `useFor: 'steel-man'` lets an unsourced, model-reasoned conclusion occupy the opposition slot
findings.expected: The opposition slot filled only by sourced material attributable to whoever holds the position; a synthesis may support it but may not stand in for it.
findings.got: `useFor` admits 'steel-man' as a destination for a conclusion, and a conclusion by this file's own opening has no direct source — its support is other cards plus an analogy. The audience sees a position where they expect the accused's answer, with a citation-shaped hole in it.
findings.refuter_pass: Reachability held at med and frequency at low: it requires the researcher to pick that `useFor` value. But nothing warns against it, and where the accused's actual words are hard to obtain it is the path of least resistance — which is exactly when it does the most damage.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether any produced conclusion is assigned useFor: 'steel-man' and whether the render attributes it.
